text:
I've written the build plan to **`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`**. Point the execution agent at that file and have it start with Phase 0. I haven't committed it.

**Your choices, as written into the plan:** a .NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid desktop app, Qdrant in Docker, the Voyage rerank API, and all four features built in phases.

**How the agent will execute:**
- **Branches and checkpoints:** each phase gets its own branch, follows the plan → you approve → build → verify loop from your slide 5, and ends with a prompt-log entry and a PR.
- **Phases:** 0 scaffold → 1 ingestion → 2 cited-answer API → 3 chat UI and plain-language mode → 4 Explain my form → 5 calculator → 6 quizzes → 7 evaluation → 8 deploy and polish.
- **Dates:** target dates run from Nov 11 to Nov 29, ahead of the demo week of Nov 30. That's tight for an empty repo.
- **Done checks:** every phase has concrete acceptance criteria the agent can check before calling it finished.

**Choices I made that weren't in your PDFs:**
- **API keys stay out of the desktop app.** The MAUI app only talks to your ASP.NET Core API, which holds the Anthropic and Voyage keys.
- **Claude returns its answer in a fixed JSON format** that tags each paragraph with a passage ID. The app's own code checks every ID and quote, which matches your slide 6 guardrail.
- **Some answers are fixed data, not AI output.** The hover definitions in plain-language mode come from a glossary file, and the "where this box goes on Form 1040" mappings come from data files. You review both, so the AI never decides either one.
- **The plan uses the `claude-opus-5-5` model.** A cheaper model, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, grades answers during evaluation.

**Your mockup has a wrong number.** Slide 11 shows tax of $1,231.50 on $12,250 of taxable income. That comes from applying the tax brackets directly. A real filer with under $100k of taxable income uses the IRS Tax Table, which calculates from the middle of each $50 row, so the answer is about $1,235. The plan tells the agent to follow the Tax Table and not copy the mockup, so your demo numbers will need updating.

**You'll still need to:**
- approve each phase's plan
- confirm each IRS PDF is the 2025 edition
- check every tax rate, deduction amount and Form 1040 line mapping I drafted
- write or approve the ~50 correct answers in the test question set
- set up the Azure, Qdrant Cloud, Voyage and Anthropic accounts and keys

Section 12 of the plan lists these, and the agent is told to stop and ask you at each one.

author: cnash03

text:
I've added tax years 2026 and 2027 to `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`, so it's ready for the execution agent. I read your "2026 and 2026" as 2026 and 2027. I took every number from the IRS's own documents: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 for 2026, and Rev. Proc. 2026-35 for 2027, which came out Nov 5.

**What the IRS has actually released so far:**
- **2026 and 2027:** only the yearly inflation-adjustment notices. These give the standard deductions, all 4 filing statuses' brackets, and the dependent deduction limits.
- **Not yet out:** the full 2026 publications (Pub 17, Pub 970 and the 2026 Form 1040 instructions with its Tax Table). They usually appear in December or January. Spring 2027 returns are for 2026, so that's the year your users will care about most.

**How the plan now handles years:**
- **Calculator:** supports 2025, 2026 and 2027, with each year's numbers in its own file, and defaults to 2026. Because the official 2026 and 2027 Tax Tables don't exist yet, it computes them the same way the IRS does and labels the result "Estimate".
- **Free tests:** each Rev. Proc. lists the exact tax at every bracket boundary, so the agent can check the calculator against about 50 numbers copied straight from IRS text.
- **Chat:** a single tax-year picker in the header. 2025 has the full set of IRS guides. For 2026 and 2027, chat answers come from the two Rev. Procs (added to the knowledge base, now 9 documents) and show a banner saying the full guides aren't out yet.
- **Adding the 2026 guides later:** add them to the source list and re-run ingestion; no code changes. Section 12, item 4a lists the steps.
- **Explain my form:** stays on 2025 until the 2026 form instructions come out, because the Form 1040 line numbers can change.
- **Calculator results:** each one notes what it leaves out: education credits, the earned income credit, and the new 2025–2028 deductions for tips and overtime. Students with tip income are told their real tax may be lower.
- **Test questions:** the evaluation set gets about 6 questions about specific years, plus 2 trick questions that check answers don't mix up years.

**Key figures:**

| | 2026 | 2027 |
|---|---|---|
| Standard deduction, single | $16,100 | $16,600 |
| 10% bracket ends at (single) | $12,400 | $12,800 |
| Dependent standard deduction minimum | $1,350 | $1,400 |

In 2027 the head-of-household top bracket starts at $661,350, $25 below the single filer's $661,375. That looks like a typo but it's what the IRS printed, and the plan copies it exactly.

You still need to hand-check every number before the calculator phase merges; the plan keeps that as a required step.

- [IRS: tax year 2027 inflation adjustments](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/irs-releases-tax-inflation-adjustments-for-tax-year-2027-taxpayers-continue-to-benefit-from-the-working-families-tax-cuts)
